title: AI-Supported Study Abroad: A Review of Emerging Evidence on Affordable Internationalization at Home
content: The cost of study abroad has been a barrier to access for a greater number of students. As a high-impact program, alternative access to study abroad should be pressing. Literature considers study abroad and artificial intelligence in isolation of each other; indicating a deeper widening research gap challenging artificial intelligence as not adequately fitted for alternate resource. Review methodology were limited to high-quality academic research databases. The findings revealed that AI has the capacity to expand access to study abroad through state agency support for institutions, and personalized learning. Access can be enhanced when institutions reverse from operating AI as an isolation, but as exploration of study abroad. Advancing AI supported study abroad programs requires greater investment in technological infrastructure and resources.
